What is being compared

has LR is read from each adapter's own declaration, not guessed. A level that differs from the sets' wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD means energies are not comparable; the tail fraction and ΔΔE slope are dimensionless shape diagnostics and stay readable.

Headline diagnostics

A correct model reads tail fraction 1, ε 0 and ΔΔE slope 1. A model with no long-range term reads 0, −1, 0. That is why these columns need no baseline to interpret.
dimers / ion_pair

Tail fraction

Slope through zero of the model's ΔE on the reference ΔE beyond 8 Å. The solid line is the correct answer; the dotted line is a model that is flat out there.

Normalised tail error ε, and the fixed-charge response

no ΔΔE data

Where the error lives

One panel per model, same axes everywhere: the shape of ε(r) separates a model that decays too fast from one that has no tail at all.

Failures and skipped blocks

A metric that could not be computed says so, which is the only way to keep an absent number from being read as a good one.oracle-refs
  • dimers: 1947 failed predictions, e.g. outside the oracle's domain (not a dimer point >= rcut)
  • dimers: charge block skipped — model outputs no per-atom charges
  • note: per-element energy offsets (fit) added to every model energy; affects only absolute energies and composition-changing differences
